  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header and date for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbat Parshat Matot and Masei,</t>
    <t s="2">Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av,</t>
    <t s="3">the year 5716*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section notes that the text is an unedited transcription.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">(An unedited transcription)</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the psalm and the Midrashic interpretation that it speaks of the future redemption, contrasting the masculine and feminine forms of song.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Halleluyah! Sing to God a new song, His praise in the congregation of chassidim,"</t>
    <t s="1">and it concludes,</t>
    <t s="2">"The exaltations of God are in their throat, and a double-edged sword is in their hand."</t>
    <t s="3">For in the verses after this, it explains what they will do with the sword, etc.</t>
    <t s="4">Now, it is brought in the Midrash Tehillim in its place that this psalm speaks about the future: Who are the chassidim? These are Israel.</t>
    <t s="5">Whenever they see the Holy One, blessed be He, they become chassidim, etc.</t>
    <t s="6">They saw Him at the sea, they became chassidim and said a song, as it is stated,</t>
    <t s="7">"Then Moshe sang," etc.</t>
    <t s="8">And when they see Him in the World to Come, they become chassidim, as it is stated, "His praise in the congregation of chassidim."</t>
    <t s="9">And so it is brought in the Mechilta and Yalkut on Parshat Beshalach that this song is for the future to come.</t>
    <t s="10">Therefore it says "a new song" in the masculine form,</t>
    <t s="11">while in many places it is stated "a new song" in the feminine form.</t>
    <t s="12">And even regarding the redemption from Egypt, it says "this song" in the feminine form.</t>
    <t s="13">And as it is explained in Shir HaShirim Rabbah</t>
    <t s="14">(on the verse "I am black but comely"):</t>
    <t s="15">A female takes a tenth of the property, etc. So Israel inherited the land of the seven nations, which is a tenth of the seventy nations, etc., they said a song in the feminine form, etc., as it is stated, "this song to God,"</t>
    <t s="16">But in the future, they are destined to inherit like a male who inherits all of his father's property, etc., they will say it in the masculine form.</t>
    <t s="17">And we need to understand the statement, "The exaltations of God are in their throat, and a double-edged sword is in their hand,"</t>
    <t s="18">for since it speaks of the future redemption,</t>
    <t s="19">then what is the matter of the sword?</t>
    <t s="20">For in the future it is written,</t>
    <t s="21">"And they shall beat their swords into plowshares... nation shall not lift up sword against nation."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
